THE GRANITE DRUM: a squat round room of thick rough grey granite in uneven courses, wide worn floorboards with a groove worn by the ladder's wheels, a timber-ribbed dome with one long slot open in it

THE HONEY-GRANITE DRUM: a round room of chunky honey-granite blocks stepping into shadow in flat dithered bands, flagstones with a timber ring set into them, a dome of ribs and boards with one long slot open up its curve

THE FROST-RIBBED DRUM: a thick rough granite drum, its courses uneven and dark between joints, wide worn floorboards, a timber-ribbed dome with frost standing in fine white lines along the inside of every board and one long slot open in it

THE SOOT-CAPPED GRANITE ROOM: a squat drum of rough grey granite in blocky stacked courses, wide boards underfoot with a great round trapdoor standing open and the stair-light coming up through it, a dome of curved ribs and boards with one long slot open

THE HOOKED GRANITE DRUM: a round room of thick rough honey-granite in uneven hard-edged courses, wide worn floorboards, a timber-ribbed dome overhead with a heavy iron hook still set into its crown and one long slot open down its side

THE WHITEWASHED DRUM: a tall round room of curving chalk-white lime-washed plaster warm where the lamp reaches it, flagstones with a timber ring set into them, a dome of painted plaster between dark ribs with one long slot open in it

THE CHALKED PLASTER ROOM: a bright whitewashed drum of curving plaster over stone, each wall-band stepping from warm white to cool shadow, wide flagstones below, a dome of dark ribs with plaster between them and one long slot open up its curve

THE IVY-RIBBED PLASTER ROOM: a round lime-washed plaster room over stone, chalk-white and warm, flagstones with a timber ring set into them, a dark-ribbed dome with ivy crept in through the slot and trailing along one rib above

THE STOVE-DRUM: a curving whitewashed plaster room over stone, warm where lamplight reaches the plaster, flagstones below, a dome of plaster between dark ribs with a small iron stove's pipe going straight up through one rib and one long slot open beside it

THE TIMBERED LOFT: a bright timber-framed room on a stone base, deep red painted posts and braces showing, wide boards underfoot, a low dome of curved ribs and boards with one long slot open up its side and a rolling ladder on an iron rail round the curve

THE AMBER-FRAMED LOFT: a timber-framed room on a stone base, amber and ochre painted posts with braces between them, wide boards underfoot, a dome of ribs and boards overhead with one long slot open in it and a great round trapdoor open in the floor below

THE BLUE-POST LOFT: a timber-framed room on a stone base, bright cobalt painted posts and pale braces, boards underfoot with a worn hollow at the ladder's foot, a dome of curved ribs and boards with one long slot standing open up its side

THE GREEN-RIBBED LOFT: a painted timber-framed room on a stone base, sage-green posts and braces in blocky pixel steps, wide boards underfoot, a dome of curved ribs and boards overhead with one long slot open and a coil of rope hung on a single timber peg

THE COPPER DRUM: a round stone room under a green copper dome, the copper seen from inside as flat verdigris sheets over curved timber ribs, wide boards with a great round trapdoor standing open in them, one long slot open up the dome's side with raw copper edges

THE COPPER-RIBBED ROOM: a drum of blocky stone courses under a dome of curved timber ribs with green copper between them, boards underfoot, a rolling ladder on an iron rail running round the curve, one long slot open in the dome with copper stepping in hard pixel bands down both sides

THE COPPER AND FLAGSTONE ROOM: a round stone drum, its courses in flat stepped shadow bands, flagstones below with a timber ring set into them, a dome of timber ribs with green copper showing at its joints and one long slot open up its curve

THE COPPER TRAPDOOR ROOM: a stone drum under a low dome of curved ribs with green copper between them, wide boards below with a great round trapdoor standing open and a coil of rope hanging in its hole, one long slot open in the dome overhead

THE LIVING-ROCK ROOM: a round room with curving cut-stone masonry on three sides and bare living rock making the fourth, flagstones below worn into a spiral of boot-hollows, a low ribbed dome of boards and ribs with one long slot open in it

THE ROCK-CROWN DRUM: a low round room built hard against raw living rock, one part of the wall bare dark stone, the rest cut masonry in uneven courses, flagstones below, a ribbed dome of boards with one long slot open up its side

THE SPLIT-WALL ROOM: a round masonry room with one deep seam of bare living rock breaking through the cut-stone courses on the west side, flagstones with a timber ring set into them, a low dome of ribs and boards with one long slot open overhead

THE ROCK-AND-PLASTER ROOM: a round room of cut masonry with one broad face of raw living rock showing through where the plaster has come away, wide flagstones below, a ribbed dome of boards with frost along its inner boards and one long slot standing open

THE MILLSTONE LOFT: a timber-framed room on a stone base with an old millstone set flat in the boards, bright painted posts and braces, a dome of curved ribs and boards with one long slot open up its side

THE BELL-HOOK TOWER: a round stone room with an old bell hook still set in the dome's crown, blocky granite courses in uneven hard-edged bands, wide worn floorboards with a round trapdoor standing open, a timber-ribbed dome with one long slot open in it

THE GRAIN-CHUTE DRUM: a round room of thick rough stone with an old grain chute closed off in the curving wall, its timber patch still dark against the stone, wide boards underfoot, a dome of ribs and boards with one long slot open and a worn groove in the boards where the ladder's wheels run

THE CONVERTED MILLROOM: a round stone room with a heavy old timber beam still crossing the curve above head height, wide boards below with an old millstone set flat among them, a low dome of curved ribs and boards with one long slot open up its side
